newsitem.title: UK: British truckers protest at Europe road anarchy.
newsitem.headline: British truckers protest at Europe road anarchy.

text.p: The UK Freight Transport Association (FTA) said it has urged the UK government to seek EU measures to protect British truck operators and drivers "from anarchy on European roads".
It said this "anarchy" is currently demonstrated in Spain and follows recent problems experienced by truckers in France and Greece.
"Today (Friday), the situation in Spain remains serious with many British trucks illegally held by Spanish strikers and with presumably no sign of a resolution to the problem," said an FTA statement.

A week-old strike is being continued by Spanish truckers, who are demanding a reduction of their retirement age to 60 years from 65, diesel subsidies, a revision of tariffs and recognition of work-related illnesses.

On Thursday, the FTA sent a letter to the UK Department of Transport stressing that "the unlawful interference with transport now taking place in Spain not only puts at risk those vehicles and drivers caught up in the action but places real economic hardship on owners".
The letter added that many of these owners had been unsuccesful in recouping losses incurred as a result of the recent similar strike actions in France and Greece.

The letter said: "It is against this background that we would formally urge the government to seek, through the Commission and the Council of Ministers, measures which will provide better protection against any further anarchy on the roads of Europe."

It said that "adequate and immediately available" compensation should be provided, through the EU, where member states would not or could not ensure the safety and free movement of international transport.
